subject: Network pathway recommendation: VPC Peering vs PrivateLink vs Site-to-Site VPN for Private pilot
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Tom Hale <thale@edgebank.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@edgebank.com>, EdgeBank NetOps <netops@edgebank.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network connectivity options for Redwood Private pilot

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with a small Redwood Private pilot but need guidance on the connectivity model. Our primary constraints:
- PII-containing inference workloads (customer data) must remain within our VPC.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 rps, occasional bursts to 1200 rps.
- Target p99 latency under 120ms for inference RPCs.
- Security team prefers minimal public exposure and wants mutual-auth + SRTP where possible.

High level ask: can you recommend whether VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or site-to-site IPSec VPN makes the most sense for our pilot and why? Please include any fallback/hybrid patterns and rough implementation steps.

I've attached a sample traffic histogram and a short SOC2 excerpt our compliance team shared. Let me know if you need anything else.

Attachments: edgebank-traffic-sample.csv; EdgeBank Network SOC2 excerpt.pdf

Thanks,
Tom Hale
Head of Cloud Engineering
EdgeBank
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Tom Hale <thale@edgebank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network connectivity options for Redwood Private pilot

Tom — thanks for the details and the attachment. Quick read-through looks helpful. Initial thoughts in short:

- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives the strongest perimeter control (no cross-VPC route advertisement) and is straightforward with least blast radius for PII workloads.
- VPC Peering is efficient for high-throughput, low-latency internal-only traffic but can complicate transitive routing and egress management across multiple accounts.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSec) is lowest friction for on-prem connectivity but usually not ideal for high sustained throughput unless you pair with BGP/MPLS and capacity planning.

I'll loop in Kim to sketch a decision matrix and an ops-focused rollout plan (MOP). Can you confirm which cloud region we should aim for (us-west-2 vs us-east-1) and whether you have a dedicated NAT/Egress proxy requirement?

— Markus
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Tom Hale <thale@edgebank.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network connectivity options for Redwood Private pilot

Tom/Markus — I put together a short pros/cons matrix and an operational recommendation based on the constraints Markus listed and EdgeBank's traffic profile.

Decision matrix (score 1-5; higher is better):
- Throughput: Peering 5 | PrivateLink 4 | S2S VPN 2
- Latency: Peering 5 | PrivateLink 4 | S2S VPN 3
- Security isolation (no public IPs): PrivateLink 5 | Peering 3 | S2S VPN 3
- Administrative surface (configuration, rotation): PrivateLink 5 | Peering 3 | S2S VPN 2
- Cost (steady-state): Peering 4 | PrivateLink 3 | S2S VPN 5
- Complexity of multi-account scale: PrivateLink 5 | Peering 2 | S2S VPN 3

Net: PrivateLink 24 | Peering 22 | S2S VPN 15

Recommendation (short):
- Primary: Use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for all inference control-plane and PII-sensitive RPCs. This keeps customer data within your VPC boundary and avoids route table propagation issues.
- Secondary (performance path): If you need lowest possible tail latency and very high sustained throughput within the same org/account, enable VPC Peering between the application VPC and the Redwood Private dataplane VPC in the same region and use it for bulk, non-PII traffic.
- Fallback: Maintain a site-to-site IPSec VPN as a disaster/fallback path or for on-premises test harnesses. Do not rely on VPN for high-volume production inference unless you provision dedicated appliances or cloud-native high-throughput VPN with LB in front.

Operational notes & gotchas:
- PrivateLink requires ENI capacity in each AZ; pick instance sizes and ENI quotas accordingly. We'll publish recommended ENI counts and a scaling table in the MOP.
- When using Peering, ensure no route overlaps; avoid transitive routing by keeping a single peering hop and using our recommended NAT/Egress pattern to centralize outbound control.
- Encryption: Mutual TLS at the application layer + mTLS termination inside the VPC. For PrivateLink, the interface endpoint is just the transport — still perform mTLS end-to-end.
- Observability: ensure flow logs at the interface endpoint and peering acceptance logs are shipped to your logging stack. We'll include a tracing header passthrough checklist.

Attachments I added: connectivity-matrix.pdf; latency-cost-estimates.xlsx; implementation-runbook-checklist.pdf

Can you confirm region (you mentioned us-west-2 in the last call) and whether EdgeBank ops requires traffic egress through a central proxy? If so, we'll fold that into the runbook.

Kim
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Hale <thale@edgebank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@edgebank.com>, EdgeBank NetOps <netops@edgebank.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network connectivity options for Redwood Private pilot

Kim — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed. Confirming:
- Region: us-west-2 for pilot.
- Egress: yes — all outbound must be via our central proxy (NAT/egress) for DLP and monitoring.

Next asks from EdgeBank side:
1) Can Redwood provide a 2-week MOP (detailed runbook) and a scoped estimate of engineering hours to stand up PrivateLink + peering fallback? (We expect a pilot in 3 weeks.)
2) We need a DocuSign for the pilot SOW (small POC fee). Please include the runbook as an annex if possible.

I've attached the SOC2 excerpt again for completeness.

Tom
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Tom Hale <thale@edgebank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network connectivity options for Redwood Private pilot

Tom — looping in a short rollout checklist and next steps. We'll prepare the MOP and SOW draft today and send a DocuSign link by EOD. High-level timeline:

- Day 0-2: Kickoff + collect IAM/region/account IDs and quota checks.
- Day 3-6: IaC + PrivateLink interface endpoint deployment (staged per AZ), ENI quota verification.
- Day 7-9: Test traffic routing via central proxy + latency/run tests; enable flow logs and tracing.
- Day 10-12: Optional peering setup in same region for non-PII bulk path; smoke tests.
- Day 13-14: Runbook handover, runbook walkthrough, and production readiness sign-off.

Deliverables: MOP PDF, IaC templates, runbook checklist, SOW/DocuSign link, and a small performance testing harness we can run together.

Related links: https://hubspot.com/deal/EDGE-1234 and internal implementation doc https://docs.redwood.com/private/implementation-runbook

We'll send the DocuSign and the detailed attachments shortly.

— Hannah
Principal Customer Engineer
Redwood Inference
